groups.sentence: Instructors word AI policies with care: welcoming, explanatory and non-punitive in tone, in plain language and without anthropomorphic wording.
Instructors discuss their AI policy and expectations with students in class at the start of the course, beyond the written syllabus.
Instructors explain to students the reasons behind their AI rules, including why AI is allowed, limited or prohibited.
Instructors discuss with students the ethical implications, risks, limitations and biases of generative AI.
Clear expectations, explanation and discussion help students understand AI rules, reduce confusion and support learning and integrity.
Instructors explain the purpose of assignments and learning goals, and why doing the work themselves matters for learning.
Instructors discuss academic integrity and plagiarism with students, including what counts as a violation when AI is involved.
Instructors invite students' questions and open dialogue about AI and the policy, and make space for students to respond.
Instructors state clearly what AI use is allowed and not allowed, with specific examples, and how use will be handled.
Instructors may use optional activities such as debates, scenarios or short comments to start AI conversations with students.
Students ask questions, discuss expectations and reflect on the ethics of AI use.
When AI misuse arises, instructors respond with supportive, transparent conversations with students before formal action.
Instructors keep reminding students of the AI policy and keep discussing it throughout the semester, not only at the start.
Institutions support open, ongoing dialogue about AI and its risks and impacts among faculty, students and the community.
